items.title: Members of public, NGOs await Tuanku Muhriz's returns
items.summary: SEPANG: The situation outside the VVIP Room at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) Terminal 1 remained calm and under control tonight as members of the public and representatives of several non-governmental organisations (NGOs) gathered ahead of the arrival of Yang di-Pertuan Besar Negri Sembilan Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir. Tuanku Muhriz is expected to arrive at 9.50pm. Those gathered were seen waiting at the terminal to welcome Tuanku Muhriz and express their support for the ruler.

items.title: AGC: Exco statement has no legal effect, move to gazette or implement proclamation on N. Sembilan Yamtuan’s removal invalid, unconstitutional
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 17 — The Attorney-General’s Chambers (AGC) said the Negeri Sembilan state executive council’s media statement or announcement has no legal effect as its members had no jurisdiction, authority or power under the Negeri Sembilan Constitution 1959 to make it. The AGC said there was also no legal basis for the state executive council members to rely on the April 19, 2026 proclamation for their announcement, adding that any move to gazette or implement the proclamation would be invalid and unconstitutional. In a statement today, the AGC said it had taken note of the document titled “Media Statement of the Negeri Sembilan State Executive Council — Decision of the Negeri Sembilan State Executive Council Meeting No.

items.title: A-GC: Negri Sembilan govt has no power to unilaterally remove Tuanku Muhriz
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Negri Sembilan menteri besar and state executive council do not have the unilateral power to terminate or vacate the position of the Yang di-Pertuan Besar, the Attorney-General's Chambers (AGC) said. In a statement responding to the Negri Sembilan government's announcement on the position of the state ruler, the A-GC said the validity and legal effect of the April 19 proclamation must be determined through the constitutional and legal process under the Negri Sembilan Constitution. The A-GC said the proclamation was invalid as it did not comply with the mandatory requirements of Article 10 of the Negri Sembilan Constitution, particularly as there was no evidence that any of the disqualifying grounds under Article 10(1) applied to Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir MORE TO COME © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Selangor allocates up to RM20mil to resolve strata title ownership issue
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: The Selangor government has allocated up to RM20 million over two years from 2025 to resolve outstanding issues involving strata title ownership in the state. Meanwhile, State Housing and Culture Committee chairman Datuk Borhan Aman Shah said the state government, through the Selangor Housing and Property Board (LPHS), had allocated RM5.68 million for three strata community empowerment initiatives in 2026. He said the initiatives comprised the CERIA Scheme, the Apartment Revitalisation and Selangor Community Strengthening (SPARK) Programme, and the C-SMART 2.0 Programme.

items.title: Pestec wins fresh injunction against Speco
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Pestec International Bhd has secured an ad interim injunction from the Kuala Lumpur High Court against Shandong Power Equipment Co Ltd (Speco). The interim injunction restrained Speco from enforcing or taking steps to enforce an undated corporate guarantee linked to an ongoing legal dispute. The legal action stems from a civil suit filed by Pestec and its subsidiaries Enersol Co Ltd and Pestec Sdn Bhd at the Kuala Lumpur High Court against, among others, Speco, Shandong Electrical Engineering & Equipment Group Co (SDEE) and certain former members of Pestech's management.

items.title: Zetrix founder Wong Thean Soon sheds 103.62mil Cuscapi shares, no longer substantial shareholder
items.summary: In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, Cuscapi said Wong disposed of about 99.12 million shares on Sept 11 while his private vehicle Asia Internet Holdings Sdn Bhd disposed of another 4.5 million shares. The total shares equaled nearly an 11 per cent stake in Cuscapi. Based on Cuscapi's closing price of five sen on Sept 11, the shares Wong disposed of totalled about RM5.18 million.

items.title: News@9: Today's top headlines - September 17, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: Wee predicts GE16 MCA president Datuk Seri Dr Wee Ka Siong says the 16th General Election could be held in four or five months. Tuanku Muhriz removed Negri Sembilan MB Datuk Ismail Lasim confirms the proclamation removing Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir as Yang di-Pertuan Besar has been approved. Rosmah appeal delayed The High Court has postponed proceedings to record additional evidence in Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor's solar corruption appeal to Nov 6.

items.title: 20 flights affected by Kota Kinabalu Airport runway closure
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The temporary closure of the runway at Kota Kinabalu International Airport has affected 20 flights today, Malaysia Airports Holdings Bhd (MAHB) said. In a statement today, MAHB said the runway remained temporarily closed to allow essential works to be completed safely, with continuous rainfall affecting the progress of the works. Passengers are advised to check their latest flight status directly with their respective airlines.

items.title: KL to create 49ha of new recreational spaces, boosts protection for green areas
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) will create nearly 49 hectares of new recreational spaces and public parks across the capital, as part of efforts to expand the city's network of green areas and recreational facilities. Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh said the strategic initiative included pre-development works and the utilisation of Department of Irrigation and Drainage reserves along Sungai Bunus and Kolam Ayer Panas. "Our main aim under this initiative is not merely to create new recreational spaces, but to ensure that every valuable open and green space in Kuala Lumpur is legally gazetted and protected," she said after inspecting the Bunus Flood Retention Pond today.

items.title: Early Kelantan polls unnecessary to prove Pas' sincerity, says deputy MB
items.summary: KOTA BHARU: Kelantan believes there is no need for the state to hold an early state election merely to prove Pas' sincerity towards Umno. Deputy Menteri Besar Datuk Dr Mohamed Fadzli Hassan said the recent state elections in Johor and Negri Sembilan had already demonstrated the party's sincerity. "The Kelantan state government is stable.

items.title: KKIA flight operations disrupted by temporary runway closure
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: Several flights at Kota Kinabalu International Airport (KKIA) were delayed, cancelled or diverted this evening following the temporary closure of its runway for rectification works. Checks by Bernama at about 5.40pm found several arriving flights from Tawau, Johor Baru, Kuala Lumpur and Guangzhou listed as delayed on the airport's flight information display. An airline source said several arriving flights had been diverted to Labuan and Sandakan following the runway closure.

items.title: #NSTviral: Superbike rider survives crash after flying into Audi's path [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A superbike rider was thrown into the path of an oncoming Audi after overshooting a corner in Jelebu, Negri Sembilan, in a crash that unfolded within seconds. A video of the incident circulating on social media showed the rider losing control while taking the bend before being flung across the road and into the Audi's lane. The Audi driver, identified on social media as Zarul, said the rider suffered a broken rib and was receiving treatment in hospital.

items.title: Reservoir Link lands RM570mil solar project, signs 30-year PPA
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Reservoir Link Energy Bhd has secured a 30-year power purchase agreement (PPA) with Syarikat Sesco Bhd for a 200MWac solar photovoltaic project in Tinjar, Sarawak, with an estimated development cost of RM570 million. Sesco is a wholly-owned subsidiary of state-owned Sarawak Energy Bhd. The project, spanning about 243.8 hectares, will be Reservoir Link's largest single renewable energy project, the company said in a bourse filing today.

items.title: Six Myanmar nationals held in RM1.2mil Lipis illegal mining raid
items.summary: LIPIS: An illegal iron ore mining site raided yesterday led to the arrest of six undocumented Myanmar nationals and the seizure of machinery and vehicles worth about RM1.2 million. The General Operations Force (GOF), together with the Pahang State Enforcement Unit (UPNP) and Lipis police, also seized seven vehicles, including five tipper lorries, an excavator and a wheel loader. GOF Southeast Brigade commander Senior Assistant Commissioner Ahmad Radzi Hussain said, acting on information, the enforcement team went to the mining site and spotted six men clearing soil.

items.title: Second body recovered as search continues for missing Pulau Ketam anglers
items.summary: Selangor Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) operations officer, Maritime Lieutenant Mohd Syafiq Sazali said a local fishing boat spotted a man’s body floating at 4.26 pm. Mohd Syafiq added that the latest recovery was about two nautical miles from where the first victim, Mohd Shahril Abd Rahman, was found yesterday. Khairul said the family is hopeful Muhammad Ridzuan is safe.

items.title: KL to add 49ha of green spaces as city moves to protect open areas, says Hannah Yeoh
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 17 — Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) will create nearly 49 hectares of new recreational spaces and public parks across the capital, as part of efforts to expand the city’s network of green areas and recreational facilities. Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh said the strategic initiative included pre-development works and the utilisation of Department of Irrigation and Drainage reserves along Sungai Bunus and Kolam Ayer Panas. “Our main aim under this initiative is not merely to create new recreational spaces, but to ensure that every valuable open and green space in Kuala Lumpur is legally gazetted and protected,” she said after inspecting the Bunus Flood Retention Pond here today.

items.title: 2 women injured as ambulance crashes into cars in Tumpat
items.summary: KOTA BARU: Two women were injured when an ambulance believed to have suffered brake failure crashed into two cars at Simpang Tiga Kampung Neting, Jalan Kota Bharu-Pengkalan Kubor, Tumpat, yesterday. Tumpat district police chief assistant commissioner Mohd Khairi Shafie said that in the 1.15pm incident, a Toyota Hiace ambulance, driven by a 43-year-old man from Kelaboran heading towards Pengkalan Kubor, experienced suspected brake failure upon reaching the location. Khairi said a urine test conducted on the ambulance driver tested negative for drugs.

items.title: Binastra's Q2 earnings soar 78pct
items.summary: Its revenue for the quarter climbed 65.9 per cent to RM658.39 million from RM396.84 million last year. The construction segment was the group's primary revenue contributor, providing RM658.2 million versus RM396.6 million a year prior. It also logged a higher pre-tax profit of RM70.6 million from RM36.3 million.

items.title: Malaysian woman, 40, dies during scuba dive in Bali’s Crystal Bay
items.summary: BALI, Sept 17 — A 40-year-old Malaysian woman died while scuba diving in the waters off Crystal Bay, Desa Sakti, Bali, Indonesia, yesterday. According to local media portal BaliNews, Siti Nuraini joined a diving trip with a dive guide, boat captain and several other divers at about 8am. However, concerns arose over her condition when the dive guide, Eugenius Franciso Ray, 33, noticed her coughing after they arrived at their first dive site at Manta Bay.

items.title: 'Mat Tok Gang' busted after nine break-ins
items.summary: SUNGAI PETANI: The 'Mat Tok Gang', which has been active in house break-ins in the Kuala Muda district since April, has been busted with the arrest of four men, including its leader. Kuala Muda police chief assistant commissioner Hanyan Ramlan said the suspects, aged between 28 and 40, were arrested during Op Pintu/Op Lejang on Sept 9 at several locations in the district, solving nine house break-in cases in Taman Delima and Taman Arked. "The Mat Tok Gang is led by a 31-year-old man who operates with three accomplices, while two other suspects, known as Nizam and Jat Chai, are still at large," he said at a press conference at the Kuala Muda district police headquarters today.

items.title: Second body recovered in Pulau Ketam angler tragedy
items.summary: Selangor Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) operations officer, Maritime Lieutenant Mohd Syafiq Sazali said a local fishing boat spotted a man's body floating at 4.26pm. Mohd Syafiq added that the latest recovery was about two nautical miles from where the first victim, Mohd Shahril Abd Rahman, was found yesterday. Khairul said the family is hopeful Muhammad Ridzuan is safe.

items.title: Malaysia offers Indonesia aircraft, helicopters to fight forest fires amid haze concerns, says Zahid
items.summary: JAKARTA, Sept 17 — Malaysia has officially offered assistance to Indonesia in tackling forest fires, including a Bombardier CL-415MP aircraft previously deployed to help its neighbour combat similar fires. Ahmad Zahid, who is also National Disaster Management Committee chairman, said the assistance would also include three helicopters and 52 officers and personnel from the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma), Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) and Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF). “We want to help Indonesia address the problem together,” he said.

items.title: Affin Bank, IFC team up on US$400mil funding for MSMEs
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Affin Bank Bhd and International Finance Corp have jointly provided greater financing access for micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) with a US$400 million financing package. The bank said the financing focuses on women-owned businesses and enterprises operating in underserved areas, aimed at broadening access to capital and strengthening support for MSMEs. Under the agreed framework, Affin Bank will channel funding to eligible MSMEs to promote productive investment, enhance business competitiveness and contribute to more inclusive economic development.

items.title: Anwar: Malaysian households using up to 800kWh exempt from AFA, Retail Charge and SST on electricity bills until Dec 31 amid haze, heat
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 17 — The government has expanded electricity bill protection for domestic users from 600 kilowatt-hours (kWh) to 800kWh a month from September to December 31, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said in a Facebook post today. He said the measure was an immediate step to ease the cost-of-living pressures faced by households, particularly as haze and hotter weather have driven up electricity consumption in some homes. He said the recent haze and warmer weather had contributed to increased electricity consumption among some households, causing their monthly usage to exceed 600kWh and resulting in unusually higher bills.

items.title: Police probe alleged road rage incident in Simpang Pulai
items.summary: IPOH: Police are investigating an incident where a car driver was allegedly threatened with a wooden stick on Jalan Ipoh-Gopeng, Simpang Pulai yesterday. District police chief assistant commissioner Muhammad Najib Hamzah said the incident occurred at 4.56pm when the victim, driving a Mercedes, claimed that his vehicle was forced to the side by a Toyota Vios before a misunderstanding arose after the victim honked at the other vehicle. The incident was also recorded by a dashboard camera (dashcam)," he said.

items.title: Construction worker dies after falling from 20th floor in Penampang
items.summary: PENAMPANG: A 20-year-old foreign construction worker died after he reportedly fell from the 20th floor of a building under construction in Jalan Bundusan here this morning. Penampang district police chief Superintendent Sammy Newton said police received a report on the incident and a team was dispatched to the site. He said officers from the Penampang district police headquarters Criminal Investigation Division, together with the Sabah police contingent headquarters D10 Forensic Unit, inspected the scene.

items.title: [UPDATED] Electricity subsidy threshold expanded to households using up to 800kWh
items.summary: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the move was an immediate measure to ease the burden on households facing higher electricity bills. Anwar said the higher threshold was necessary as hotter weather and haze had led some households to increase their electricity consumption, pushing their monthly usage above the previous 600kWh threshold. "These conditions have driven higher electricity consumption among some households, causing their monthly usage to exceed 600kWh and resulting in unusually high electricity bills," he said in a statement today.

items.title: Malaysia offers Indonesia Bombardier aircraft, assets to tackle forest fires — Zahid
items.summary: JAKARTA: Malaysia has officially offered assistance to Indonesia in tackling forest fires, including a Bombardier CL-415MP aircraft previously deployed to help its neighbour combat similar fires. Zahid, who is also the national disaster management committee chairman, said the assistance would also include three helicopters and 52 officers and personnel from the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma), Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) and Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF). "We want to help Indonesia address the problem together," he said.

items.title: Police probe Simpang Pulai road rage after Mercedes driver allegedly threatened with stick
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 17 — Police are investigating an incident where a car driver was allegedly threatened with a wooden stick on Jalan Ipoh-Gopeng, Simpang Pulai, near here, yesterday. Ipoh district police chief ACP Muhammad Najib Hamzah said today that the incident occurred at 4.56pm when the victim, driving a Mercedes, claimed that his vehicle was forced to the side by a Toyota Vios before a misunderstanding arose after the victim honked at the other vehicle. The incident was also recorded by a dashboard camera (dashcam), he said.

items.title: MARKET PULSE PM SEPT 17, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia's benchmark index closed lower on Thursday dragged by weakness in petrochemical, telecommunications and banking counters. The key index dropped nearly five points to 1,674 at the closing bell. In the crypto exchange, Bitcoin rose to RM314,140.

items.title: Ipoh woman loses RM41,215 in online job and fake investment scams
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 17 — A 36-year-old woman lost RM41,215 after falling victim to an online job scam and a non-existent investment scheme recently. Muallim district police chief Supt Khalid Mohamad said the victim received a job offer through WhatsApp on September 13, with rewards offered for completing product evaluation tasks on the Shopee platform. He said the victim was subsequently instructed to make several money transfers to bank accounts provided by the suspect.

items.title: Glomac swings back to black with RM7.6mil net profit in Q1
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Glomac Bhd returned to the black in the first quarter ended July 31, 2026 with a net profit of RM7.6 million from a loss of RM1.42 million a year ago. Its revenue for the quarter under review more than doubled to RM68.53 million from RM26.05 million in the same period last year. Revenue from the property development segment for the current quarter rose RM41.9 million, mainly due to increased development activities in ongoing projects.

items.title: [UPDATED]: Good news on electricity bills coming soon, says Anwar
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has hinted at good news regarding the issue of higher electricity bills that have burdened some households. Anwar said a statement on the matter would be issued soon. Anwar chaired an hour-long special meeting to discuss measures to mitigate the impact of higher electricity bills on households.

items.title: KLIA is world's fourth most connected international megahub
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Kuala Lumpur International Airport has retained its position as the world's fourth most connected international megahub and ranked first in OAG's 2026 Low-Cost Megahubs Index. AirAsia said its Its extensive network links Kuala Lumpur with destinations across Asean, Asia and Australia, contributing significantly to the airport's connectivity. Bo Lingam, group chief executive officer of AirAsia Group, said KLIA's ranking reflected the network built by the airline and its cooperation with Malaysia Airports Holdings Bhd (MAHB).

items.title: Tasek Ipoh records country's highest API reading at 186
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Tasek Ipoh in Perak recorded the country's highest Air Pollutant Index (API) reading at 186 as of 6pm today. Samarahan in Sarawak recorded 168, while Johan Setia in Selangor recorded 165. Meanwhile, 33 stations recorded moderate air quality, with readings ranging from 51 to 100.

items.title: ‘Stare’ case at Kepong restaurant: AGC reviewing technician’s representation over grievous hurt charge
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 17 — The Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC) is still reviewing a representation by a technician seeking reconsideration of a charge of causing grievous hurt to a man in a “stare” incident at a restaurant in Kepong here in May. Deputy Public Prosecutor Adiba Iman Hassan said the representation by second accused Lai Kae Bin was submitted on September 2 and is still under consideration. On May 14, Lai, 33, carpenter Wong Weng Luen, 49, and memorial centre worker Wan Ken Fei, 30, pleaded not guilty to intentionally causing grievous hurt to Andrew Teh Tiek Hua, 49, at a restaurant in Jalan Kepong, Metro Prima, at 2am on May 7.

items.title: IGP: Police DNA lab logs 420 matches, seeks more technology for forensic investigations
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 17 — The enhancement of the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) DNA Analysis Laboratory through a RM11.1 million allocation under the 12th Malaysia Plan (12MP) has enabled PDRM to carry out 420 Deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) matching cases, including those involving serious crimes. Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail, however, said PDRM still required additional logistics, equipment and technology to further strengthen its investigative capabilities and help solve more cases that require forensic analysis. Mohd Khalid said other departments and agencies needing forensic analysis assistance could also use the PDRM Forensic Laboratory’s expertise, adding that the increased allocation would enable the adoption of more new technologies in the future.

items.title: 'Not a sundry store': Aminuddin calls for firm stance amid crisis
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Former Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun has urged the state leadership to maintain a clear and firm stance, warning against changing positions during royal institutional crises. He said the state leadership must avoid inconsistent positions that could lead to repeating past mistakes. Aminuddin's remarks follow conflicting positions on the status of Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir as the Yang di-Pertuan Besar Negri Sembilan.

items.title: Foreign worker compliance challenges
items.summary: Enforcement may catch the problem but prevention is what keeps the system orderly. And here, the Foreign Workers Centralised Management System (FWCMS) deserves more attention than it usually receives. FWCMS offers one answer.

items.title: Couple's final breakfast before fatal motorcycle convoy crash [WATCH]
items.summary: Mohd Zamri Mohd Zaki, 41, and Norlyana Ismail, 45, were killed in the 9.45am accident. Convoy participant Md Faizal Md Yusof, 52, said he had known the couple for only a month. He said the group of 12 Aveta Nova 250 motorcycles left Kuala Terengganu at 7.30am and were heading to Kuala Perlis.

items.title: No evidence of established piranha population in Pahang’s Klau Dam yet, says Fisheries Dept
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 17 — The Department of Fisheries (DOF) said today there is no evidence yet of an established or breeding piranha population in the Klau Dam, Raub, following the catch of a fish suspected to be of the species on August 26. Fisheries director-general Datuk Adnan Hussain said only one such fish had so far been reported caught in the area, while investigations and field monitoring by the Pahang Fisheries Department up to September 15 found no additional catches or related safety incidents. He also said that releasing alien fish species that could become invasive into public waters was irresponsible as it could adversely affect inland aquatic ecosystems, local fish populations and aquatic biodiversity.

items.title: Haze: 30 areas across Malaysia record unhealthy air quality, including Ipoh, PJ, Shah Alam and Kuching
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 17 — A total of 30 areas nationwide recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 5pm today. According to the Malaysia Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, Tasek Ipoh in Perak recorded the highest reading at 188, while three other areas in the state also had unhealthy API readings, namely Seri Manjung (179), Pegoh Ipoh (158) and Taiping (155). In Sarawak, three areas recorded unhealthy readings: Kuching (172), Serian IPD (172) and Samarahan (167).

items.title: Vodus study: Anwar records highest acceptance, first-choice support among PM hopefuls
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 17 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has emerged as the strongest overall candidate for the prime ministership in a new national study by Vodus Research, recording the highest public acceptance, first-choice support and net acceptance among five prominent prospective candidates. The Malaysia Prime Minister Candidate Study 2026 found that 46 per cent of respondents aware of the candidates said they would accept Anwar as prime minister, while 34 per cent named him as their first choice. His net acceptance score stood at +19 percentage points, also the highest among the five candidates surveyed.

items.title: Army steps up drone surveillance on border routes amid unrest in southern Thailand
items.summary: MELAKA, Sept 17 — The Malaysian Army (TDM) is using advanced drone technology to strengthen security monitoring in hard-to-reach areas along the Malaysia-Thailand border, particularly in response to the unrest in southern Thailand. Chief of Army Gen Tan Sri Azhan Md Othman said the technology enabled TDM to overcome the challenges posed by hilly and densely forested terrain, where physical patrols by troops were difficult. Azhan also gave an assurance that border security remained tight, with round-the-clock operations in place.

items.title: KLIA ranks first in Asia for connectivity in OAG Megahubs 2026 ranking
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 17 — Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KUL) ranked fourth globally and first among all Asian airports in OAG’s Megahubs 2026 ranking, with connections to 154 destinations, while also topping the Low-Cost Carrier (LCC) Megahubs index with nearly 15,000 possible low-cost connections. OAG, the intelligence partner for global travel, said its annual ranking of global airport connectivity showed Asia Pacific (APAC) dominating the index, with eight airports in the global top 20. According to OAG in a statement, AirAsia operates 34 per cent of total flights at KUL, while Seoul Incheon ranked second in the LCC rankings with connectivity reaching 198 destinations.

items.title: Kota Kinabalu airport runway temporarily closed for rectification works
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 17 — The runway at Kota Kinabalu International Airport has been temporarily closed to facilitate rectification works, Malaysia Airports Holdings Bhd (MAHB) said today. In a notice on Facebook, MAHB said a Notice to Airmen (NOTAM) had been issued over the temporary closure. “The runway will reopen once the necessary safety inspections and clearing works have been completed,” it said.

items.title: Papagomo fails to stay RM280,000 defamation payout to Lim Guan Eng, son
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 17 — The High Court today dismissed an application by Wan Muhammad Azri Wan Deris, better known as Papagomo, to stay the execution of a judgment ordering him to pay RM280,000 in damages to former Penang Chief Minister Lim Guan Eng and his son. On May 19 this year, the court ruled that Wan Muhammad Azri was liable for defamation and ordered him to pay RM280,000 in damages to Guan Eng and Clint Lim Way Chau over the latter's posts alleging that Way Chau was detained in Singapore for purportedly bringing in RM2 million in undeclared cash in 2020. The court ordered the defendant to pay global damages of RM200,000 and costs of RM30,000 to Guan Eng as well as damages of RM80,000 and costs of RM10,000 to the second plaintiff (Way Chau).

items.title: Palm oil mill shut down after pump failure sends effluent into Johor’s Sungai Sembrong
items.summary: KLUANG, Sept 17 — A palm oil mill in Kluang has been identified as the source of pollution in Sungai Sembrong and ordered to halt operations immediately. “Further investigation revealed a pump malfunction at the mill’s effluent treatment pond, causing an overflow of oil-contaminated effluent into Sungai Sembrong. The DoE reminded industries, particularly palm oil mill operators, to strictly comply with requirements under the Environmental Quality Act 1974 and the department’s licensing conditions.

items.title: BPHB unit appointed Bintulu Port operator for 30 years
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 17 — Bintulu Port Authority (Sarawak) has appointed Bintulu Port Holdings Bhd's (BPHB) wholly-owned subsidiary Bintulu Port Sdn Bhd (BPSB) as an approved port operator for Bintulu Port for 30 years, from September 1, 2026 to August 31, 2056. “The appointment is set out in the Bintulu Port Authority (Sarawak) (Appointment of Approved Port Operator) Notification, 2026, published in the Sarawak Government Gazette, Part II, dated September 10, 2026. On June 23, 2026, the Sarawak Ministry of Infrastructure and Port Development notified BPSB that the government had approved in principle the appointment of BPSB as the approved port operator for Bintulu Port under Section 12(2)(a) of the Port Authorities Ordinance, 1961.

items.title: PMO says letter claiming Cabinet approval for PLUS highway widening is fake
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 17 — The Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) today said that a letter dated July 17, 2026, claiming that Cabinet approval had been given for a proposed Private Finance Initiative (PFI) project to widen the North-South Expressway (PLUS) is fake. In a statement today, PMO stressed that the Prime Minister had never issued or signed the letter and denied any connection with the document or the purported approval. “PMO has lodged a police report over the forgery of the document and the misuse of the Prime Minister’s name and PMO’s official identity.

items.title: Critics of Anwar should back their words with action, says PKR Youth chief
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 17 — PKR Youth chief Muhammad Kamil Abdul Munim has hit out at those criticising Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, saying some were quick to make political statements but lacked the courage to follow through with their actions. He said while there were political statements suggesting that the country was currently unstable, the government remained committed to ensuring political stability as a foundation for economic stability and, ultimately, the benefit of the people. “Our priority is to ensure political stability because from there, we can ensure economic stability, which will ultimately benefit the people,” he said.

items.title: Melaka assembly dissolution date still undecided, says CM
items.summary: ALOR GAJAH, Sept 17 — The date for the dissolution of the Melaka State Legislative Assembly to pave the way for the state election has yet to be set, said Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh. Ab Rauf, who is also Melaka Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman, said several state administrative matters needed to be resolved first to ensure all plans proceeded smoothly before the assembly was dissolved. The Melaka State Assembly has 28 seats, while the current state government's mandate expires on December 31.

items.title: Court of Appeal stays Rosmah’s additional evidence hearing pending Federal Court appeal
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 17 — The Court of Appeal today allowed the prosecution’s application to stay the hearing of additional evidence from a key prosecution witness in Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor’s corruption case involving the RM1.25 billion Sarawak solar hybrid project. “With the consent of both parties, we allow the application to stay the Court of Appeal’s order dated September 1 until the prosecution’s appeal is disposed of by the Federal Court. On September 1, the Court of Appeal allowed Rosmah’s application to adduce additional evidence in her appeal against her conviction and sentence.

items.title: Quit if you no longer recognise Tuanku Muhriz as ruler, Loke tells Negeri Sembilan exco members
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Sept 17 — DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke Siew Fook today called on Negeri Sembilan executive council members to resign if they no longer recognise Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir as the state’s Yang di-Pertuan Besar. Yesterday, the state Exco announced that it regarded an April 19 proclamation removing Tuanku Muhriz from the throne as valid and recognised Tuanku Nadzaruddin Tuanku Ja’afar as the new Yang di-Pertuan Besar with immediate effect. Loke said Tuanku Muhriz could not be removed from the throne without going through the process required under the state constitution.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan MB instructs state secretary to gazette Tuanku Muhriz’s removal despite DKU objection
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 17 — Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim has instructed the state secretary to proceed with gazetting the removal of Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir as Yang di-Pertuan Besar, despite the Dewan Keadilan dan Undang (DKU) saying the state executive council has no jurisdiction to determine the ruler’s position. According to Free Malaysia Today (FMT) Ismail told reporters after an event in Seremban that he endorsed the statement issued by the state executive council yesterday affirming Tuanku Muhriz’s removal. The exco’s statement yesterday affirmed that Tuanku Muhriz’s removal in April was legitimate and that Tuanku Nadzaruddin Tuanku Ja’afar was the new ruler of Negeri Sembilan.

items.title: Kedah fertiliser company managing director released on MACC bail
items.summary: ALOR SETAR, Sept 17 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) in Kedah has released the managing director of a fertiliser supplier company who was remanded in connection with the delay in the distribution of Supplementary Compound Fertiliser supplies to paddy farmers in the state. Meanwhile, Kedah MACC director Datuk Nazli Rasyid Sulong, when contacted, confirmed the matter and said the suspect had been released on MACC bail. Previously, the MACC opened an investigation paper regarding the issue of delayed distribution of Paddy Fertiliser 3 to paddy farmers in Kedah.

items.title: Global energy shock now hitting Malaysia’s electricity costs, says economy minister
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Sept 17 — Global energy supply disruptions are now exhibiting a lagging effect, as the impact, concentrated on the petrol market since last March, begins to spread to natural gas and coal. Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said the lagging effect is beginning to impact electricity generation costs directly, particularly for consumers whose monthly electricity usage exceeds 600 kilowatt-hours (kWh). “Natural gas is a fuel that is burned to generate energy.

items.title: Soldier charged with kicking five-year-old daughter at Kelantan eatery
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Sept 17 — A soldier was charged in the Sessions Court here today with abusing his five-year-old daughter by kicking her at an eatery in Jalan Kuala Krai last Friday. According to the charge, the accused allegedly kicked the girl at an eatery at Lot 143, Batu 2, Jalan Kuala Krai, here at 10.55pm on September 11, 2026. Earlier, the prosecution did not offer bail, citing concerns that the accused could interfere with the victim, who is also his biological daughter.

items.title: Puchong blaze guts four factories, collapse risk remains (VIDEO)
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 17 — A fire destroyed four factories at Jalan TPP 5/15, Puchong Industrial Park, today. Selangor Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) assistant director of operations Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the department received an emergency call at 6.34am. He said the fire affected a total area measuring 80 by 100 feet, involving four premises comprising a tyre factory, a hardware factory for pipes and valves, a furniture factory and an engineering factory.
